title: Why Sewer Gas Enters Buildings: Unsealed P-Traps
description: Sewer gas entering a building is frequently caused by a dry or siphoned P-trap. The P-trap holds a standing pool of water that acts as a physical barrier against sewer main vapors. When a fixture remains unused for extended periods, the water inside the trap evaporates. Alternatively, improper venting causes negative pressure or siphoning that pulls the trap seal down the waste line. Without this liquid barrier, toxic and foul-smelling sewer gases freely escape through the drain opening. Inspecting fixture usage, trap primers, and proper DWV venting prevents dry trap failures and maintains safe indoor air quality.

Why Sewer Gas Enters Buildings: Unsealed P-Traps

Sewer gas entering a building is frequently caused by a dry or siphoned P-trap. The P-trap holds a standing pool of water that acts as a physical barrier against sewer main vapors. When a fixture remains unused for extended periods, the water inside the trap evaporates. Alternatively, improper venting causes negative pressure or siphoning that pulls the trap seal down the waste line. Without this liquid barrier, toxic and foul-smelling sewer gases freely escape through the drain opening. Inspecting fixture usage, trap primers, and proper DWV venting prevents dry trap failures and maintains safe indoor air quality.
